title: Bangladesh Liberation War and the surrender of 16 December 1971
summary: The Pakistan army began a crackdown on Dhaka on the night of 25 March 1971, and a nine-month war for Bengali independence followed. On 16 December 1971 Pakistani forces in the east surrendered at Dhaka to the Mukti Bahini and the Indian Army. Death-toll estimates run from 300,000 to 3 million; about ten million people fled to India.

uncertainty.note: Start is the night of 25 March 1971 (Operation Searchlight, around 11 pm per The Daily Star); independence was proclaimed on 26 March, not sourced on opened pages. End is the surrender on 16 December 1971.

where.modern_name: Dhaka, Bangladesh (the war covered all of former East Pakistan)
where.historical_name: Dacca, capital of East Pakistan, Islamic Republic of Pakistan

importance.justification: War that created Bangladesh and one of the deadliest conflicts of the late twentieth century.

audience_note: Describes mass killing, rape and displacement of civilians. Death-toll figures are contested and politically sensitive.

related.because: East Pakistan, the territory that became Bangladesh, was created by the 1947 Partition.

sources.title: The grim numbers of 1971: Genocide versus denial

reviewer_note: Casualties: "most estimates" 300,000 to 3 million (The Daily Star, 2007), R. J. Rummel about 1.5 million (same page), "upwards of 3 million" (Amnesty USA). The official Bangladeshi figure is 3 million; Pakistani official figures are far lower but were not on an opened page. Surrender was signed at Ramna Race Course, Dhaka, per search results only. beats.caption: The Pakistan army attacked sleeping residents of Dhaka around 11 pm in an operation it called Searchlight.
Pakistani forces surrendered to the Mukti Bahini and the Indian Army, ending the war.
